h1: The 6 Best Cartridge-Free Printers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six cartridge-free tank printers from Epson and Canon, compared on document feeders, connectivity and who each suits.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-3850 is the best overall cartridge-free printer for home offices. The ET-2800 is the pick for light home printing, the ET-4950 suits heavier office use, and the Canon PIXMA G620 is the choice for photos.
intro: Cartridge-free does not mean ink-free. These printers swap the tiny cartridge for a refillable tank you top up from a bottle, and the real decision is whether you need a document feeder and wired networking or just a compact printer for occasional pages.

We reviewed eight tank printers and ranked six on listed features: automatic document feeders, scanning, Ethernet, touchscreens, ink supply and size. Duplicate colour variants were folded into one entry, and the premium office model sits outside this shortlist.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-3850 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A feeder, scanner, Ethernet and a bonus ink bottle make it the best balance.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-3850 combines an automatic document feeder, scanner and copier, Ethernet and mobile printing support in a refillable tank design. A bonus black ink bottle and USB cable are included.

It ranks above the ET-4950 because it keeps the useful office tools while avoiding the touchscreen and speed-oriented extras that raise the price tier. Against the ET-2800 below, you gain the feeder and wired network.

Buy it if you scan multi-page documents or share a printer across a household. The caveat is that it sits in the $200 to $500 bracket, more than the entry models.
products.idealFor: Home offices that scan and copy multi-page documents.
products.skipIf: You print a few pages a month.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4950 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A touchscreen, feeder and rated three years of ink refills for heavier use.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-4950 adds a 2.4-inch colour touchscreen and an automatic document feeder, with an 18 ppm print speed and ink refills rated for up to three years. It is designed for people who print regularly.

It ranks second because the ET-3850 does the core jobs for less, so you are paying for the screen and speed. Against the ET-4850, it skips the fax focus and leans on the display.

Pick it for a busy home office. The caveat is that the rating of three years assumes typical use, not heavy printing.
products.idealFor: Busy home offices printing every day.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest cost per printer.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer (Black)
products.verdict: A compact print, scan and copy printer with ink bottles included for setup.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is a compact wireless all-in-one that prints, scans and copies, and ships with ink bottles for setup. It sits in the $100 to $200 tier.

It ranks below the ET-3850 because it has no listed document feeder or Ethernet port. You trade office tools for a smaller, cheaper machine.

It fits students and occasional printers. The caveat is that scanning multi-page documents means placing each sheet on the glass by hand.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4850 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Fax, Ethernet and a feeder in an office-oriented white body.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-4850 includes fax, Ethernet, an automatic document feeder, scanner and copier in a white, office-oriented design.

It ranks below the ET-4950 because it lacks the touchscreen and speed detail, though it matches the feature set otherwise. Fax is the reason to choose it.

Pick it for a business that still sends faxes. The caveat is that most households never use the fax line.

products.name: Canon PIXMA G620 Wireless MegaTank Photo All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: A photo-focused MegaTank printer that works with Alexa.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA G620 is a refillable MegaTank photo all-in-one that prints, copies and scans with wireless connectivity and Alexa support. It targets photo output rather than documents.

It ranks below the Epson office models because the listing shows no feeder, so it suits photos over paperwork. It is the only Canon here, a useful alternative to Epson.

Choose it for photo prints. The caveat is that it is not built for stacks of document scanning.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A compact everyday EcoTank for simple home printing.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 is a compact wireless print, scan and copy printer built for everyday home printing, with the refillable tank system.

It ranks last because the listing is plain next to the ET-2800, with no setup ink detail. The two are close, so pick on current availability.

Choose it for simple needs. The caveat is that it has no feeder or Ethernet in the listing.

whatMatters.detail: A tank printer holds ink in a reservoir you refill from a bottle, replacing small cartridges. This usually lowers running cost for regular printers. Check the listing for the words EcoTank or MegaTank and see whether setup ink is included.
An automatic document feeder pulls multi-page originals through the scanner. Without one you place every page on the glass by hand. Look for the feeder in the bullets, not the photos.
Ethernet gives a stable connection for shared printers, where Wi-Fi may drop. It matters if several people print. Check the listing for an Ethernet port.
Speed is listed in pages per minute and affects long jobs. The ET-4950 lists 18 ppm. Look for a number in the specs, since vague words such as fast do not help.
Fax support adds cost and matters mainly for legacy business workflows. Most homes can skip it. Confirm in the listing whether fax is built in.

howToChoose.intro: Match the machine to your habits.

cards.label: Epson EcoTank
cards.text: Broad lineup with feeders and Ethernet. The ET-3850, ET-4950, ET-4850, ET-2800 and ET-2400 are all Epson.

cards.label: Canon MegaTank
cards.text: Photo-focused with Alexa support. The Canon PIXMA G620 is the one Canon in this ranking.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to Epson unless photos matter most.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: An automatic document feeder, scanner and wired networking for steady use.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Epson EcoTank ET-3850 has all three plus a bonus ink bottle.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print daily and want the touchscreen and speed of the Epson EcoTank ET-4950.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print occasionally, where the Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is enough.

faq.a: The printer uses a refillable ink tank instead of cartridges. You pour ink from bottles into the tank.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Skipping the feeder. If you scan more than a page or two, a model without one gets tedious.

faq.q: Is the ET-3850 worth it over the ET-2800?
faq.a: Yes if you scan documents or want Ethernet. If not, the ET-2800 does the basics for less.
The ET-2800 and ET-3850 list included bottles. Check each listing before relying on it.

faq.q: How do I fill the tanks?
faq.a: Match the bottle colour to the tank and pour carefully. Follow the setup guide in the box.
They all print in colour, but the Canon PIXMA G620 is the one aimed at photos.

finalTake: The Epson EcoTank ET-3850 is the cartridge-free printer most home offices should buy. Step up to the ET-4950 for daily use, drop to the ET-2800 for light printing, and choose the Canon PIXMA G620 if photos matter. Decide on the feeder first and the rest follows.
